Investing in training programs that offer practical experience and connect employers to trainees—for example, by enhancing contractors’ capacity to host interns or apprentices—can effectively bridge the gap between job seekers and employers, thereby expanding contractor capacity to implement building efficiency projects. The findings from this national survey highlight how building efficiency contractors make decisions about hiring and training. These decision-making processes may vary from other industries, based on the nature of work, business economics, and specific challenges for building efficiency employers. There could also be regional variations in different parts of the country, urban versus rural areas, or in states or jurisdictions that have different building and energy programs, or energy efficiency incentive or other programs. Workforce development and training program administrators should always undertake a more local needs assessment that includes contractor engagement before developing or rolling out new programs.
